name: Oktoberfest '96 (Night 1)

date.source: the card's own dateline, "Reported on Friday, October 25 1996", and the Prodigy message headers running through the document, each dated 10/25/96

appearances.note: Billed by the card's own announce desk for the SuperDome Sweet Dreams tag team main event, as Dr. Silver's chosen Dream Partner. The match is not in the surviving copy of the card.

Billed by the card's own announce desk for the SuperDome Sweet Dreams tag team main event, with an unnamed Dream Partner, and for a United States title match on the second night. Neither is in the surviving copy of the card.
Billed by the card's own announce desk to defend the AAWC Universal Tag Team titles with Kurt Taylor against the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels. The match is not in the surviving copy of the card.
Billed by the card's own announce desk to defend the AAWC Universal Tag Team titles with Shawn Matthews against the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels. The match is not in the surviving copy of the card.

Billed by the card's own announce desk against the Generation X-Press; after Saafir Muhammed was arrested backstage the booth said 187 might have to wrestle it alone. The match is not in the surviving copy of the card.

matches.note: Van Justice's AAWC debut. He caught Massacre mid-plancha and dropped him with a stun gun on the ringside railing, then rolled him in and pinned him.
Payne attacked before the bell, ramming Havok headfirst through the glass of a giant jukebox at ringside, and finished with a top-rope powerbomb. Havok hit The Turntable on him after the match.
Windsor was accompanied by Stevie Rogers and the Silver Beetle, hired to impersonate Anarky and Thomas Gunn. Gunn pinned Windsor after Windsor was knocked into Rogers and cracked heads with him.

Booked as Ultra Violent vs. the Vegas Connection; when Ultra Violent could not be found after a blackout, Dr. Silver came to the ring and substituted his own Elite Guard. Bloodhunt pinned Gage after the Fall of Saigon, and hit it on Reno as well once the match was over.
Vai reversed the figure four, and Spanky Richards baited Rair into catching a thrown steel chair and kicked it into his face. Vai pinned him after the Pain Killer.

The Untouchables and Nathan Storm jumped Arrogance in the aisle before the bell; Storm put Peyton Wright through the Spanish broadcast table, and Wright took no part in the match. Melton wrestled alone, opened Knight up with a chain and rolled him up, and Palmer came in and reversed the small package for the win.

For the AAWC Television Championship, under the fed's own stipulation that the first man to pin anybody wins the belt. Bloodhunt tagged himself in as Taylor hit the Lex Plex, hit Taylor with the Headshot, tagged Virile's arm and rolled the unconscious challenger on top of the champion for the count. Dr. Silver's whole group came out afterwards and handed Virile the belt.
matches.title: aawc-television

matches.note: For the AAWC United States Heavyweight Championship. Both men were opened up, Randalls by his own hand with a broken table leg to break the Fashion Statement; Price tried to walk out and was sent back by President Schmid. The surviving copy of the document ends mid-count on a Price small package, so the record does not name a winner.
matches.title: aawc-united-states-heavyweight

notes: Night one of the AAWC's own two-night Oktoberfest, subtitled SUPERDOME SWEET DREAMS, posted to the Prodigy service's WRESTLING BB in twenty-nine numbered parts. The document is held as NFW republished it in its own news archive; the served page carries the Prodigy message header verbatim at the head of every part, with redactions where the poster's own identifier stood. The capture is incomplete — it ends mid-count during the United States title match, and the announced SuperDome Sweet Dreams main event, Universal Tag Team title defence and 187 vs. Generation X-Press match are not in the surviving text. The card's own announce desk counts "eight other matches for you here tonight, including three title matches" beside the main event — nine in all, of which the surviving copy carries eight, the last of them unfinished.

name: Oktoberfest '96 (Night 2)

date.source: The first night's own dateline, "Reported on Friday, October 25 1996", plus that card's own repeated billing of the second night as "tomorrow night" at "this two-night event."

evidence.note: President Schmid, from the ring: "He is our United States Heavyweight champion, and he has two top-notch title defenses lined up for this very event. Tonight, he steps in that ring with Mike Randalls. Tomorrow night, he steps into that ring with Mike Chain."
The announce desk on the Randalls/Adler booking: "tomorrow night's NIGHTMARE IN NEW ORLEANS match with 'I Quit' rules."
On Scottie Vai: "now he has to sit and wait to see whether his matchup with Xavier Virile tomorrow night will be for the AAWC Television title."
On the Untouchables: "Benjamin Palmer and Jason Knight will now move on to face the AAWC Universal Tag Team champions, whomever they may be, tomorrow night right here at OktoberFest."
Dr. Silver, on the guest commentator he had a chair brought out for: "I'd hate for him to complain that he lost to me tomorrow night because his ass was sore from a rock hard chair."

Billed by the fed's own President, from the ring, to challenge for the AAWC United States Heavyweight title.

Billed by the announce desk for a NIGHTMARE IN NEW ORLEANS match against Mike Randalls under "I Quit" rules.

notes: The second half of the AAWC's own two-night Oktoberfest '96, billed all through the first night and not held in any form. Every appearance here is a billing and nothing more: no copy of this card is known to survive, and nothing held says whether it ran. The first night also floats a possible AAWC Television title match for Mark Windsor on this card — "a possible match", never announced — which is why he is not billed here.

name: Nitro (Three Rivers Stadium)

date.source: The Oktoberfest '96 card of 25 October 1996 places it "last week in Pittsburgh" and "earlier this week" throughout.

evidence.note: The card's own opening video package: "Footage from Nitro in Pittsburgh, with Dr. Silver standing face to face with Tom Adler... Adler and Randalls brawling throughout Three Rivers Stadium... Price getting his hand raised in victory after winning the United States title in Pittsburgh."
On the AAWC United States Heavyweight title change: "newly crowned United States champion 'Fashion Plate' Marcus Price", who won the belt in Pittsburgh the week before.

On Joe Massacre: "Massacre was impressive in his debut last week in Pittsburgh, but that was spoiled by Bloodhunt, when Bloodhunt outsmarted the AAWC newcomer by goading him into smashing him with a chair in full view of the referee, earning a disqualification."
On Flic Rair: "looking to redeem himself after last week's controversial loss to Steve Masters on Nitro"; and on Scottie Vai, "He beat Anarky last week."

On the Silver/Adler match: "that very controversial match they had in Three Rivers Stadium, which resulted in a full-scale RIOT", Silver having walked out after pinning Adler "for a fifty-five count with Adler's own move."
On Arrogance: "We haven't heard much from Arrogance since they attacked Shawn Matthews last week in Pittsburgh."

notes: The AAWC's own weekly show, named Nitro by its own commentary, running from Three Rivers Stadium in Pittsburgh the week before Oktoberfest '96. Six separate results from it are narrated on the held card — a United States title change, a debut, a disqualification, two singles losses and a backstage attack — and no copy of the show itself is held. Whether all six belong to one Pittsburgh card or to more than one is not stated; the held card speaks of "last week in Pittsburgh" as a single occasion.

name: WrestleFest '95

date.source: A CSWA retrospective's own Hornet/GUNS timeline dates "AAWC Wrestlefest" to May 1995 (promotions/cswa/archive/cswa-spotlight-hornet-vs-guns-1998.html).

evidence.note: The card's own opening: "the presidency of the AAWC was sold to CS Enterprises at the end of WrestleFest by former president Robert Schmid."

The card's own opening video package: "Footage from Wrestle Fest. GUNS walking down the aisle and getting attacked by Tully Planchard and Ern Enderson. CUTTO: Dr. Silver with GUNS in the Body Cast, GUNS refusing to give up... CUTTO: Tom Adler celebrating after winning the Universal title."
On the Schmid/Teri Melton storyline: "she dumped him after his loss to Tom Adler at WrestleFest."

The Oktoberfest '96 card's own commentary, more than a year later, still dating things by it: Dr. Silver "outsmarted Price at WrestleFest", and "Price had that knee injured at the hands of Dr. Silver at WrestleFest."

The same retrospective calls it the AAWC's "premiere event": "The featured event: the creation of an AAWC Universal Champion, merging the AAWC World Title with the AAWC Unified Title (created from a previous merge of three of the AAWC's lesser titles). The event featured GUNS, Hornet, Doctor Silver and Flic Rair. The first man to defeat his three opponents in consecutive matches would become the new champion."
The same timeline's own line for the card: "AAWC Wrestlefest / May 1995 / Hornet def. GUNS / AAWC Universal Title on the line."

notes: The AAWC's own supercard, named by both held AAWC cards and held in neither. Four results are narrated across the two: Tom Adler beat President Robert E. Schmid and won the AAWC Universal Heavyweight title, the presidency of the AAWC was sold to CS Enterprises at the end of the show, GUNS was beaten after a Planchard and Enderson attack and a Dr. Silver Body Cast, and Dr. Silver beat Marcus Price and injured his knee. A CSWA retrospective describes the main event as a four-man round robin among GUNS, Hornet, Dr. Silver and Flic Rair and does not name Tom Adler; the AAWC's own card of 5 August 1995 replays Adler's WrestleFest title celebration and bills him as the reigning Universal Champion. The two accounts are recorded side by side.

name: World War Games 3

date.source: Billed as upcoming in the Prodigy Wrestling BB's own FW Central league register of 9 July 1997, and reported as having happened "in just the last two days" in the board's own headlines of 22 July 1997.

evidence.note: The register's own AAWC entry: "The All Action Wrestling Conference continues their annual tradition of heading overseas to wage war when they arrive in Wembley Stadium for their third annual World War Games," followed by the full announced card.

The board's own headlines of 22 July 1997: "in just the last two days, the AAWC World Title changed hands once again at World War Games 3. Former AAWC World Champ Steve Masters took the title from Scotty Michaels in a special stipulation added during the match."
The board's own Unified Championship rankings of 22 July 1997, listing "Steve Masters -- AAWC World Champion" and "Anarky -- AAWC US Champion".

Also billed and not registered here: the AAWC Universal Tag Team title match between the Dirty Rotten Scoundrels and Dawn of a New Day, whose champion the record does not name, and El Toro, unminted. The first two World War Games are attested only by this card's own "third annual" and by the AAWC's own World War Games of March 1995.

name: AAWC's UNDER NEW OWNERSHIP

matches.note: For the AAWC Universal Tag Team Championship. Billed as ARROGANCE, accompanied by Teri Melton, challenging THE ARMED FORCES, led by TTL. Ruled a double disqualification for the interference of Steven Flair and GUNS; the champions kept the belts. The document declares neither a draw nor a no contest, so no result field is set. The finish spilled into a ringwide brawl involving Steven Flair, GUNS, Tom Adler and Alexandr Karelin.

matches.stipulation: tuxedo match, with one million dollars on the line
matches.note: Stipulation as read out: the only way to win is to strip your opponent to their underwear. Schmid is billed as the former President of the AAWC, who sold the presidency to CS Enterprises and was then double-crossed into this match.

Non-title, one fall, thirty minute time limit; the CS Express are billed as EN and CPUWA World Tag Team Champions. Two decoys in Western outfits stood in the ring while the real Cutters attacked from behind before the bell, Enderson hitting Morton's shoulder with the timekeeper's bell; the announcers call it a broken collarbone and Gibson worked most of the match alone. Morton returned taped up and pulled Planchard into Enderson's top-rope drop, and Gibson small-packaged Enderson.

notes: RE-FILED UNDER AAWC, 2026-09-02, because a show document of one fed served in another wing's archive files its show row under the fed that STAGED it — the lot 0033 pattern (the id was cswa-aawcs-under-new-ownership-1995-08-05). The card is titled AAWC's UNDER NEW OWNERSHIP, it stages the AAWC Universal Tag Team and AAWC Universal Heavyweight Championships, and the CSWA's own broadcast calls it "the AAWC's final card". THE DOCUMENT STILL SERVES IN THE CSWA WING and `page` still points at that copy (/promotions/cswa/archive/aawcs-under-new-ownership-1995-08-05.html, lot 0062); it is on CSWA's own holdings page and stays there. IT IS GENUINELY CO-PROMOTED: the same card also stages CSWA's own EN World Heavyweight Championship, in the double-title cage main event, and a CS Express non-title tag match — which is why the CSWA-side reign cswa-en-world-heavyweight-c003 still cites this row as its event, now across the two wings. THE SHOW-ID MACHINERY HAS NO ALIAS OR REDIRECT: data/aliases.json carries retired ids for CHARACTERS and UNITS only (registry-validate resolves an alias target against the entity index), and shows have no per-show page to redirect — only year indexes — so the old id is simply gone and every reference to it was repointed by hand. APPEARANCE-LEVEL TENURES WERE NOT REWRITTEN by the re-file: this registry already attributes tenure by what the text stages rather than by the show's filing — battleship-cswa and submarine-cswa already carried aawc tenures for this date because they wrestled for an AAWC title, while the CS Express and the broadcast team carry cswa ones — and that reading survives the move unchanged. Recorded, not silently altered.
